subject: Acme MAP: mutual action plan & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood-inference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme MAP: mutual action plan & next steps

Hi Laura & Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on pain, goals, stakeholders, and next steps. Please reply with any corrections or additions and I’ll update the MAP spreadsheet.

Pain points we heard
- High per-request latency on current embeddings pipeline (~400-600ms) causing poor search UX.
- Cost volatility on peak batch loads; procurement wants predictable unit economics.
- Data governance: need VPC/private deployment option for PII use cases and SOC 2 evidence for procurement.

Goals / success criteria
1) Reduce tail latency to <200ms for search flows at P95.
2) Reduce per-token/embedding cost by 30% through batching + model profile recommendations.
3) Complete security review (SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration) and procurement sign-off by end of Q3.

Key stakeholders and roles (as discussed)
- Evaluation / Technical: Laura Chen (Search Product Lead), Tom Wu (Search Eng)
- Procurement / Legal: Procurement team (procurement@acme.com)
- Executive sponsor: (TBD) — Laura to confirm

Decision process & timeline
- Technical POC (3 weeks) -> Security review (2 weeks overlapping) -> Procurement & SOW negotiation (2-3 weeks) -> Final decision.
- Target decision date: 2026-09-15 (customer provided this as their internal target).

Milestones (proposed)
- Week 1 (Aug 3–7): Kickoff + scoping call with Redwood SE (Rishi) and Acme eng 
- Week 2–3 (Aug 10–21): POC deployment + baseline perf metrics
- Week 4 (Aug 24–28): POC results review + joint perf tuning
- Week 5–6 (Aug 31–Sep 11): Security evidence submission + procurement review

Open questions / blockers
- Laura: need list of SOC 2 artifacts and expected timelines from our security team.
- Tom: will Acme allow temporary VPN/peering for the POC or prefer sample data in a sanitized bucket?

Next steps (owner / date)
- I’ll share the MAP spreadsheet and a draft SOW (attached). (Marissa) — sent now.
- Rishi to schedule a 60-minute kickoff with your eng team next week. (Rishi)
- Laura to confirm executive sponsor and procurement SLA expectations by Aug 6. (Laura)

Attachments: 20260801-acme-map-v1.xlsx (MAP draft), SOW-draft-acme.docx

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood-inference.com | (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Acme MAP: mutual action plan & next steps

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few items from our side: 

1) Timeline tweak: The 3-week POC window is fine but could you confirm availability for Aug 11–25 for the bulk of testing? That aligns better with our sprint schedule.

2) Security artifacts: procurement wants our standard SOC 2 checklist and any pen test reports. Can you share a checklist and expected delivery timeline for those items?

3) Data access for POC: We prefer to avoid opening VPC peering for the initial POC. Instead, we can provide a sanitized sample dataset (anonymized search logs) hosted in a secure S3 bucket. Will that work?

4) Procurement contact: looping in procurement above. They’ll want your standard SOW + pricing sheet.

Looking forward — if you can adjust the MAP dates to reflect Aug 11 start, that’d be great.

Tom
Senior Engineering Manager, Search
Acme Corp
